styles.name: Pilsner
styles.taste: Crisp and dry, with grainy malt and a noticeable floral or herbal hop finish.
styles.say: Crisp and refreshing, with a clean finish and a little hop bite.
styles.pairing: Seafood, fried appetizers and light salads

styles.name: Light lager
styles.taste: Light-bodied and highly refreshing, with mild malt and very little bitterness.
styles.say: A light, easy-drinking lager with a mild flavor.
styles.pairing: Light appetizers, sandwiches and salty snacks

styles.name: Pale lager
styles.taste: Clean, smooth malt with a restrained hop finish; fuller than many light lagers.
styles.say: A clean, smooth lager with a little more malt flavor.
styles.pairing: Burgers, pizza and grilled chicken

styles.name: Mexican lager
styles.taste: A broad serving category of crisp pale lagers from Mexico; individual recipes differ.
styles.say: A crisp, easy-drinking Mexican lager.
styles.pairing: Tacos, grilled seafood and chips with salsa

styles.name: Amber lager
styles.taste: Toasty malt and a smooth finish; Oktoberfest and Vienna examples vary in sweetness and strength.
styles.say: A smooth lager with toasted malt and a little more richness.
styles.pairing: Roast pork, sausages and burgers

styles.name: Dark lager
styles.taste: Toasted or lightly roasted malt, with a clean lager finish; dark color does not imply high strength.
styles.say: Dark in color, but smooth and lighter than you might expect.
styles.pairing: Grilled meats, mushrooms and roasted vegetables

styles.name: Bock & doppelbock
styles.taste: Malt-led lagers with bread, toast or caramel; doppelbocks are usually richer and stronger.
styles.say: A malt-forward lager; check the beer because strength varies widely.
styles.pairing: Roast meats, aged cheese and hearty stews

styles.name: Kölsch
styles.taste: A delicate, pale ale with a crisp finish and subtle fruity notes.
styles.say: As refreshing as a lager, with a subtle fruity edge.
styles.pairing: Seafood, salads and delicate chicken dishes

styles.name: Wheat beer
styles.taste: A broad family: German examples often taste of banana and clove; American wheat ales can be much cleaner.
styles.say: A refreshing wheat beer with a softer malt feel.
styles.pairing: Salads, chicken and mild cheeses

styles.name: Belgian-style wheat
styles.taste: Soft wheat character, often with citrus and spice, and a light, refreshing finish.
styles.say: A refreshing wheat beer with citrus and spice.
styles.pairing: Seafood, salads and citrus-led dishes

styles.name: Saison
styles.taste: Dry, lively and often peppery, with fruity yeast character and high carbonation.
styles.say: A dry, lively farmhouse ale with fruity and peppery notes.
styles.pairing: Roast chicken, goat cheese and herb-led dishes

styles.name: Belgian ale
styles.taste: Yeast-led fruit and spice; pale strong ales, dubbels and quadrupels have different malt profiles.
styles.say: A fruity, spicy ale with plenty of character.
styles.pairing: Rich meats, aged cheese and roast dishes

styles.name: Blonde ale
styles.taste: Approachable, lightly malty ales, usually with restrained bitterness.
styles.say: An easy-drinking ale with light malt and gentle bitterness.
styles.pairing: Chicken, sandwiches and light appetizers

styles.name: Cream ale
styles.taste: A light, smooth American ale-lager tradition; the name does not mean it contains cream.
styles.say: A smooth, mild beer; cream ale refers to the style, not a cream ingredient.
styles.pairing: Sandwiches, burgers and fried appetizers

styles.name: Pale ale
styles.taste: Hop-led ales, often with citrus or pine, balanced by malt; bitterness varies.
styles.say: A hoppy ale with some malt balance, usually less intense than a stronger IPA.
styles.pairing: Burgers, grilled food and cheddar

styles.name: IPA
styles.taste: Hop-forward, often with citrus, pine or resin and a dry or malt-balanced finish.
styles.say: A hop-forward beer with a noticeable bitter finish.
styles.pairing: Grilled food, burgers and sharp cheese

styles.name: Hazy IPA
styles.taste: Cloudy, often softer in texture, with tropical or citrus hop aromas; bitterness is still possible.
styles.say: A juicy, hop-forward IPA with a softer feel and tropical or citrus notes.
styles.pairing: Grilled chicken, tacos and aromatic dishes

styles.name: Double IPA
styles.taste: A stronger, more intense hop-forward ale; malt and alcohol can add fullness.
styles.say: A stronger IPA with concentrated hop flavor.
styles.pairing: Rich grilled food and strong cheese

styles.name: Amber & red ale
styles.taste: Toasty or caramel-like malt, with a balanced hop finish; American and Irish examples differ.
styles.say: A malt-balanced ale with toasted or caramel notes.
styles.pairing: Burgers, roast chicken and cheddar

styles.name: Brown ale
styles.taste: Nutty, toasted and caramel-like malt, sometimes with a light cocoa note.
styles.say: A smooth brown ale with nutty, toasted malt flavor.
styles.pairing: Roast pork, mushrooms and nuts

styles.name: Porter
styles.taste: Dark ales with chocolate, coffee or toasted malt; usually less roast-sharp than a dry stout.
styles.say: A dark ale with chocolate and coffee-like malt flavors.
styles.pairing: Barbecue, roast meats and chocolate desserts

styles.name: Stout
styles.taste: Roasted malt, coffee and cocoa; dry, milk and oatmeal versions differ in sweetness and texture.
styles.say: A dark, roasted beer; check whether this version is dry, sweet or smooth.
styles.pairing: Oysters, roast meats and chocolate desserts

styles.name: Imperial stout
styles.taste: Full-bodied, rich roasted malt and higher alcohol; barrel-aged versions may add vanilla or oak.
styles.say: A rich, stronger stout with concentrated roasted flavor.
styles.pairing: Chocolate desserts and strong cheese

styles.name: Sour beer
styles.taste: Tart or sour beers with varied fruit and fermentation character; a gose may add a salty edge.
styles.say: A tart, refreshing beer; ask how sour and fruity the guest likes it.
styles.pairing: Salads, seafood and soft cheese

styles.name: Fruit beer
styles.taste: Fruit-forward beers spanning sweet, dry and tart; check the individual beer rather than assuming sweetness.
styles.say: A fruit-led beer; this particular one may be sweet or tart.
styles.pairing: Fruit desserts, soft cheese and salads

styles.name: Non-alcoholic
styles.taste: Commercial low- or no-alcohol beers in several styles; a non-alcoholic label can still mean less than 0.5% ABV.
styles.say: A lower-alcohol option; check the label if the guest requires 0.0%.
styles.pairing: Choose pairings by the beer’s lager, wheat or hop-forward profile
